ch11.d.mode: Pull the string down through the hole to shorten the radius, or let it out to lengthen it
ch11.d.rIn: Radius with the string pulled in; the outer radius is 1 m
ch11.d.wOut: Angular velocity on the 1 m circle; sets the angular momentum $L$
ch11.d.areas: Sectors swept by the string in equal time intervals; all have the same area
ch11.s.goal.L: The string pulls towards the hole, so its torque about the hole is zero and the angular momentum $L = mr^2\omega$ is conserved
ch11.s.goal.K: Angular momentum is conserved but kinetic energy is not: the force pulling the string does work
ch11.s.obs.flat: $L(t)$ stays flat even while the string is being pulled
ch11.s.obs.square: Half the radius: four times the angular velocity ($\omega \propto 1/r^2$)
ch11.s.obs.work: $K(t)$ rises when the string is pulled in and falls when it is let out; the rise equals the work done by the pulling force
ch11.s.obs.area: Swept areas: sectors swept in equal times have equal areas, whether long and thin or short and wide (the same principle as Kepler's second law, Ch 13)
ch11.s.obs.release: Let out: as the radius grows, $\omega$ falls while $L$ stays the same
ch11.s.assume: Frictionless table, massless string, point-like puck; the string is worked so that the radius changes smoothly over a fixed time; seen from above
